title: 9 Best Semantic Layer Tools For AI Agents In 2026
summary: The best semantic layer tools for AI agents in 2026: Malloy (our pick), dbt MetricFlow, LookML, Power BI, Cube and AtScale, with MCP support and pricing.
body_markdown:
## What a semantic layer does for AI agents


A semantic layer stores business definitions once and compiles every request into SQL that follows them, turning "write correct SQL against a large schema" into "pick a metric and a few dimensions". It doesn't decide which metric the person meant ([the semantic layer solves the wrong half](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/the-semantic-layer-solves-the-wrong-half) ); our[semantic layer guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/semantic-layer) covers the evidence on both sides.


## How I compared them


On definitions, query interfaces, MCP support, whether row-level security reaches the agent, pricing and portability, from vendor docs and pricing pages read in October 2026 plus building Dot's connectors for six of them. I ran no head-to-head accuracy benchmark, so Malloy's place at the top is a design recommendation, not an accuracy ranking.


## 1. Malloy (our pick)


**Best for:** any team that can choose its semantic layer: one open-source, code-first language for the model and the queries, with no BI platform to buy.


Malloy is an open-source modeling and query language ([MIT, on GitHub](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy) ) co-created by Looker founder Lloyd Tabb ([Santa Cruz Works](https://www.santacruzworks.org/news/looker-founder-helps-create-new-data-exploration-language-malloy) ). The startup Credible builds a commercial product on it ([VentureBeat](https://venturebeat.com/data/57-of-enterprises-traced-a-wrong-ai-answer-to-missing-business-context-credible-bets-portable-open-source-semantic-code-beats-proprietary-metadata) ).


- **Why it's our pick:** measures are names, not formulas; aggregates stay correct across joins; the compiler catches mistakes before the warehouse does; and a restricted mode keeps LLM-written queries inside the model. Our Malloy guide makes the full case.
- **Interfaces:** Malloy compiles to SQL for your warehouse. Its[README](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy) lists nine database engines, including BigQuery, Snowflake, Postgres, DuckDB/MotherDuck and Trino (as of October 2026). Publisher, Malloy's open-source model server, serves models over REST and MCP ([malloydata/publisher](https://github.com/malloydata/publisher) ).
- **MCP and AI:** Publisher has a built-in MCP server at` localhost:4040/mcp` with tools such as` get_context` ,` compile_model` and` execute_query` ([README](https://github.com/malloydata/publisher) ). The endpoint has no authentication: the docs recommend binding it to 127.0.0.1 and putting an authenticating gateway in front of anything wider ([Malloy docs](https://docs.malloydata.dev/documentation/user_guides/publishing/mcp_agents) ).
- **Pricing:** free and open source. You pay for the warehouse, and for hosting Publisher if you run it.
- **Limitations:** a young project with a small ecosystem, so business users need a front end you build or buy, and Publisher and its MCP server are younger than the long-running commercial layers (as[Cube's own comparison](https://cube.dev/articles/open-source-semantic-layer) notes).


## 2. dbt Semantic Layer (MetricFlow)


**Best for:** teams whose transformations already live in dbt and who want metrics reviewed and versioned next to the models.


MetricFlow, the engine that turns a metric request into SQL, has been open source under Apache 2.0 since October 2025 ([dbt Labs](https://www.getdbt.com/blog/dbt-labs-affirms-commitment-to-open-semantic-interchange-by-open-sourcing-metricflow) ); the dbt Semantic Layer is dbt Labs' hosted service around it. Metrics are YAML in your dbt project ([latest spec](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/latest-metrics-spec) ).


- **Interfaces:** JDBC, ADBC and GraphQL APIs, plus a Python SDK ([Semantic Layer APIs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/dbt-apis/sl-api-overview) ).
- **MCP and AI:** dbt Labs maintains an open-source MCP server ([dbt-labs/dbt-mcp](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-mcp) ) that runs locally or remotely, with Semantic Layer tools such as` list_metrics` ,` query_metrics` and` get_metrics_compiled_sql` . The remote server is on every dbt platform plan, but which tools you get depends on the plan ([dbt MCP docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/dbt-ai/about-mcp) ).
- **Pricing:** MetricFlow is free. The hosted Semantic Layer comes with the Starter, Enterprise and Enterprise+ plans ([dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/use-dbt-semantic-layer/dbt-sl) ). Starter lists at $100 per developer seat a month and includes 5,000 queried metrics a month; Enterprise is custom-priced and includes 20,000 ([dbt pricing](https://www.getdbt.com/pricing) ,[Paradime's 2026 summary](https://www.paradime.io/guides/dbt-cloud-pricing) ).
- **Limitations:** an agent can only answer what is modeled as a metric. Query caching and multiple credentials per project are Enterprise features ([Semantic Layer FAQ](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/use-dbt-semantic-layer/sl-faqs) ). Setup and the MCP route: our dbt Semantic Layer guide.


## 3. Cube


**Best for:** one metric layer that serves BI tools, spreadsheets, embedded analytics and AI agents at once.


Cube Core is the open-source, headless semantic layer (Apache 2.0); Cube Cloud is the managed platform built on it ([GitHub](https://github.com/cube-js/cube) ,[Cube docs](https://cube.dev/docs/product/administration/distribution) ). Metrics live in YAML files that declare cubes and views.


- **Interfaces:** REST, GraphQL and SQL APIs ([Cube docs](https://docs.cube.dev/docs/introduction) ). An MDX API for Excel on Windows (Enterprise plan, preview;[MDX API](https://cube.dev/docs/product/apis-integrations/core-data-apis/mdx-api) ) and a DAX API for Power BI (public preview;[Cube blog](https://cube.dev/blog/cube-for-the-microsoft-enterprise) ) connect over XMLA.
- **MCP and AI:** Cube Cloud hosts an MCP server with OAuth on its Premium and Enterprise plans. It exposes 30 tools, nine of them destructive ([Cube MCP docs](https://docs.cube.dev/docs/integrations/mcp-server) ); self-hosted Core relies on community MCP servers.
- **Pricing:** Cube Core is free. Cube Cloud has a free tier, and paid plans combine per-user seats with metered compute. Third-party listings put Starter at about $40 and Premium at about $80 per user a month but disagree on the compute rates, so get a quote; Enterprise is custom ([TrustRadius](https://www.trustradius.com/products/cube-js/pricing) ,[Gartner Peer Insights](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/product/cube-platform) ).
- **Limitations:** two meters make the bill harder to predict, and self-hosted Core gets REST, GraphQL and SQL only, run and secured by you.


## 4. Looker (LookML)


**Best for:** Google Cloud and BigQuery teams that already run Looker and want agents to reuse its explores.


LookML views define dimensions and measures, explores define how views join, and Looker compiles every query into SQL.


- **Interfaces:** the Looker API and its SDKs; the Open SQL Interface, which exposes LookML models to any tool that supports JDBC ([Google docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/sql-interface) ); and the Conversational Analytics API, generally available for BigQuery and Looker since June 23, 2026 ([release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/conversational-analytics-api/release-notes) ).
- **MCP and AI:** the Looker-managed MCP server is in preview and built into Looker-hosted instances, at your instance URL plus` /mcp` . Every tool is off until an admin enables it, and the client inherits the user's Looker roles ([Looker MCP docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/mcp) ). Customer-hosted instances use Google's open-source MCP Toolbox for Databases ([Google docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/connect-ide-to-looker-using-mcp-toolbox) ).
- **Pricing:** platform editions plus role-based user licenses on an annual commitment, through sales ([Looker pricing](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) ; estimates in our[Looker pricing breakdown](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-pricing) ).
- **Limitations:** the model is only queryable through Looker, so its value depends on keeping a Looker license. The managed MCP server is a preview without OAuth scopes or dynamic client registration, and an agent that ignores an explore's default filters can override them by accident.


## 5. AtScale


**Best for:** large enterprises where Excel and Power BI users need live, governed metrics on a cloud warehouse, without extracts.


AtScale is a commercial universal semantic layer. In 2024 it open-sourced its YAML-based modeling language, SML, under the Apache license ([BusinessWire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240910415282/en/AtScale-Announces-the-Open-Source-Release-of-SML-A-Standard-Semantic-Modeling-Language) ), and it joined the Open Semantic Interchange in January 2026 ([BusinessWire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260127372541/en/AtScale-Joins-the-Open-Semantic-Interchange-OSI-Bringing-over-a-Decade-of-Semantic-Layer-Expertise-to-support-Open-Standards) ).


- **Interfaces:** Power BI and Excel connect live over XMLA with DAX and MDX, Tableau and Looker over JDBC and ODBC, Python notebooks through AI-Link ([AtScale](https://www.atscale.com/use-cases/business-intelligence/) ).
- **MCP and AI:** AtScale's MCP server has been in the Databricks MCP Marketplace since December 1, 2025 ([AtScale](https://www.atscale.com/press/atscale-databricks-mcp-marketplace-semantic-layer/) ). AtScale says row-level security and column masking apply to agents as to BI users ([AtScale blog](https://www.atscale.com/blog/enterprise-ai-mcp-semantic-layer/) ).
- **Pricing:** consumption-based, priced on deployed semantic objects. At its 2024 launch AtScale advertised plans "as low as $2,500 per month"; real quotes are custom ([BusinessWire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240606134196/en/AtScale-Announces-Next-Generation-Product-Now-Generally-Available-with-Consumption-Based-Pricing-and-Free-Trial) ).
- **Limitations:** built for large BI estates rather than a five-person data team, and the accuracy figures in AtScale's material come from its own tests.


## 6. Power BI semantic models


**Best for:** Microsoft shops where DAX measures already define the business and people read them in Power BI, Excel and Teams.


Tables, relationships and DAX measures that reports read live; our[Power BI semantic model guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/power-bi-semantic-model) walks through an example.


- **Interfaces:** DAX queries over the XMLA endpoint, which only works on workspaces on Fabric capacity, Premium capacity or Premium Per User, and is read-only by default ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/enterprise/powerbi/service-premium-connect-tools) ); and DAX through the Power BI REST API.
- **MCP and AI:** Microsoft's remote Power BI MCP server (preview) reads a model's schema and generates and runs DAX. The user needs Build permission, and row-level security applies when users sign in but not with a service principal ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/developer/mcp/remote-mcp-server-tools) ). Microsoft now points question answering to its generally available, read-only Fabric IQ MCP server (our Power BI MCP guide), and the open-source Authoring MCP server (formerly the Modeling MCP server) lets an agent change models and run DAX, capped at 100,000 rows ([GitHub](https://github.com/microsoft/powerbi-modeling-mcp) ).
- **Pricing:** Power BI Pro is $14 and Premium Per User $24 per user a month, billed annually ([Microsoft](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing) ). Outside tools that read models over XMLA, Dot's connector included, need PPU, Premium or Fabric capacity. Our[Power BI pricing guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/microsoft-power-bi-pricing) has the capacity math.
- **Limitations:** outside Microsoft's own tools, only clients that speak XMLA and DAX can use the model, and the capacity requirement raises the floor for small teams.


## 7. Snowflake semantic views


**Best for:** teams that keep everything in Snowflake and use Cortex Analyst or Cortex Agents.


A semantic view is a schema-level Snowflake object with tables, relationships, facts, dimensions and metrics, created in SQL or from a YAML spec ([CREATE SEMANTIC VIEW](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/create-semantic-view) ,[querying](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/views-semantic/querying) ).


- **Status:** querying semantic views became generally available in August 2025 ([release 9.25](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/2025/9_25) ), and naming a semantic view in a plain` FROM` clause went GA on March 2, 2026 ([release note](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/2026/other/2026-03-02-semantic-views-standard-sql) ).
- **MCP and AI:** the Snowflake-managed MCP server can expose Cortex Analyst as a tool, and only over semantic views ([Snowflake docs](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp) ); it returns generated SQL, not results ([Snowflake guide](https://www.snowflake.com/en/developers/guides/getting-started-with-snowflake-mcp-server/) ).
- **Pricing:** we found no separate price for the views themselves. Cortex Analyst bills AI credits when called through Cortex Agents or per 1,000 messages through its standalone API, and running the SQL uses warehouse compute ([Cortex Analyst docs](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-analyst) ).
- **Limitations:** definitions live inside Snowflake, so outside tools need a bridge such as AtScale.


## 8. Databricks metric views


**Best for:** Databricks lakehouse teams that use AI/BI dashboards and Genie.


Metric views are defined in YAML in Unity Catalog. Measures must use aggregate functions and are queried with` MEASURE()` , and` SELECT *` isn't supported ([Databricks docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/business-semantics/metric-views/yaml-reference) ).


- **Status:** generally available as part of Unity Catalog Business Semantics, which Databricks is also open-sourcing; materialization is still in preview ([Databricks blog](https://www.databricks.com/blog/redefining-semantics-data-layer-future-bi-and-ai) ). External BI tools can query them too ([Databricks docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/business-semantics/metric-views/bi-tools) ).
- **MCP and AI:** Databricks' managed MCP servers include Genie One, generally available since September 2026, a Genie Agent server scoped to one agent, and Databricks SQL ([Databricks docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/mcp-tools/managed-mcp) ,[Databricks blog](https://www.databricks.com/blog/genie-one-mcp-now-generally-available) ).
- **Pricing:** we found no separate price; you pay for the Databricks compute that runs the queries.
- **Limitations:** Databricks only, and every column has to be listed explicitly.


## 9. Steep


**Best for:** teams that want metrics, a metric catalog and an exploration UI in one product.


A metrics platform with its own semantic layer that can also sit on top of the dbt Cloud Semantic Layer ([Steep docs](https://help.steep.app/integrations/dbt-cloud) ) or Cube ([Steep](https://steep.app/) ).


- **Interfaces:** the Steep API, launched on January 20, 2026, exposes the metrics and semantic model you define in Steep ([Steep](https://steep.app/blog/introducing-steep-api) ).
- **MCP and AI:** a hosted MCP server at` https://mcp.steep.app/mcp` since May 28, 2026, with OAuth; an agent only sees data you can see in Steep ([Steep changelog](https://steep.app/changelog/mcp) ).
- **Pricing:** third-party listings disagree, so check[Steep's pricing page](https://steep.app/pricing) .
- **Limitations:** it is metrics-first, so a question that no defined metric covers is out of scope.


## Others worth knowing


- **Honeydew:** a semantic layer that runs as a Snowflake Native App ([Honeydew](https://honeydew.ai/blog/why-did-we-build-a-native-app-for-honeydew-semantic-layer-on-snowflake) ). Its text-to-data API is also available through a Honeydew MCP server ([Honeydew docs](https://honeydew.ai/docs/integration/context-layer/api) ), and it publishes per-user pricing ([pricing](https://honeydew.ai/pricing/) ).
- **GoodData:** an analytics-as-code BI platform with its own semantic layer. Its MCP server, announced in January 2026, lets AI create, change and validate semantic models, metrics and dashboards ([GoodData](https://www.gooddata.com/press-releases/gooddata-announces-launch-of-mcp-server) ). Pricing is through sales.
- **Open Semantic Interchange (OSI):** not a tool but a vendor-neutral format for moving definitions between these layers, now Apache Ossie; see our OSI guide for which tools support it.


## How to choose a semantic layer for your stack


### If you can choose: Malloy


If you can choose, choose Malloy. It costs nothing to license, and GetDot reads it natively ([Malloy integration](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/malloy) ). The cases below are the exceptions, where switching is unrealistic and the layer you run should stay.


### Looker shops: keep LookML


If Looker is your BI tool, keep the definitions in LookML so every Looker surface and outside agent computes revenue the same way. Malloy, co-created by Looker's founder, keeps LookML's core idea, so a large LookML estate can move to it gradually, starting with new models. See the[Looker](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/looker) integration page and our[Gemini in Looker comparison](https://www.getdot.ai/compare/looker-vs-dot) .


### Microsoft: Power BI semantic models


If your measures already exist in DAX, don't rebuild them in a second layer; fix descriptions and relationships first, because every AI client reads the same model. Copilot or an outside analyst? See our[Power BI Copilot comparison](https://www.getdot.ai/compare/powerbi-vs-dot) .


### dbt shops: the dbt Semantic Layer


If you are committed to dbt, MetricFlow keeps metric definitions in the same pull requests as the models, and the dbt MCP server gives agents` query_metrics` without extra glue. The catch is that the hosted APIs need a paid dbt plan.


### Many BI tools or embedded analytics: Cube or AtScale


When the same metric has to reach Tableau, Power BI, Excel, your own product and an agent, a universal layer earns its cost: Cube for engineering-led teams (open core, APIs, pre-aggregations), AtScale for enterprises whose heaviest users live in Excel and Power BI.


### All in on Snowflake or Databricks


Semantic views and metric views are the cheapest place to start if every consumer sits inside that platform. Once a second BI tool or an outside agent needs the definitions, you're back to a bridge or a second layer.


### No semantic layer yet


Don't start with a tool. Write down what your top 20 metrics mean and which table is the source of truth, then make the ones people argue about deterministic, in Malloy unless your stack already settles it. Our[semantic layer guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/semantic-layer) covers when you need one, and[AI made that second step cheap](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/ai-made-the-semantic-layer-cheap) .


## How AI analysts use these layers


1. **The layer's own MCP server.** Quick and governed for modeled metrics, but it only sees its own layer, so a question that crosses systems or needs an unmodeled table stalls or gets guessed.
2. **The platform's own assistant** (Gemini in Looker, Copilot in Power BI, Cortex Agents, Genie): strong inside one platform, blind outside it.
3. **A governed AI analyst that reads the layer.** It queries the layer for defined metrics and the warehouse for everything else, keeps the context the layer can't hold (which metric people mean, known data issues), and answers where people work.
